_doc_walkSceneKey: the town's EXPLORABLE scene key — stated role, not inferred (district fixed-camera bundles carry the whole town's collision, so pad names cannot identify the walk scene). This is the real-time DEVELOPER view; the game routes players into playSceneKey. Built by tools/emb_blockout.py. | REPOINTED 2026-08-01 (camera lane, 2x round): was `emb-walk`, a one-off tools/emb_export.py bundle last written 07-31T04:43 against the 1x town — every camera solved against it was solved against a town that no longer exists (its walk bounds max out at x 31 where the map now runs to x 118). `emb-townwalk` is the SAME master exported by the ten-minute cron (tools/townwalk_live_refresh.sh -> tools/town_export.py), so the walk geometry the solver measures is the geometry the blockout currently builds: 162 walk_ meshes at 2x against emb-walk's 139 at 1x. emb-walk is left on disk as the superseded bundle and is named by nothing.
_doc_playSceneKey: the scene the GAME sends players to — the town played as a sequence of FIXED pre-rendered shots (the FF grammar this project exists for). Deliberately separate from walkSceneKey: the real-time bundle stays the developer's explore view, and which of the two the scene graph wires is a data choice, not a naming coincidence.
_doc_cameraFile: the hand-authored camera INTENT for playSceneKey. tools/cine_solve.mjs --town emberbrook solves it against this map + the walkSceneKey walk geometry (emb-townwalk) into emberbrook.cameras.solved.json — the one numeric truth cine_bake.py and play3d.html both read.
premise: The home village: a valley farming settlement gathered around its living Heartlight — one of the last — where the village brook meets the river. Warm, low, earthbound; everything Dellhollow is not. The river is the story's spine: Vesper arrives along it, and leaves through the Sigil Gate to follow it downstream.
units: world units (1u ~ 1m). Axes: x = west-east, y = south-north, z = height (village sits on a gentle rise, z 0..3).

mapDiscovery.rule: Entering a parcel's scene reveals it and its mapVisible landmarks (Vesper inks the map as she walks).

_doc_landmark_footprint_doorFace: TWO OPTIONAL LANDMARK FIELDS, both stamped 2026-08-01 on the dressing lane's measurements.
`footprint`: [W, D, wallHeight] in metres, the building's own body. emb_blockout reads it in
place of its per-class literal, and BOTH the massing and bodysize() use it — which matters
because the DOORSTEP is derived by pushing out from the landmark past that body's half-depth.
The watermill's 2x re-rule moved the building and not the literal, so the mill's own walk pad
ended up 1.12 m INSIDE the dressed footprint: a doorstep for a building that no longer existed.
Any landmark whose built size stops matching its class default should carry this field rather
than have a second literal added to the builder.
`doorFace`: a COMPASS BEARING IN DEGREES (0 = +y, 90 = +x) naming the outward normal of the wall
the door is in. A bearing rather than a face token, because a landmark is yawed to its own site,
so 'the south wall' is only meaningful against a rotation the map does not otherwise state; a
bearing is checkable with one measurement. It exists because the doorstep is derived from the
ARRIVING EDGE's bearing while the door is built into a wall, and the two can disagree —
measured at the watermill as 34 degrees, which is the kind of almost-right a player reads as
wrong. Where a landmark carries it, the builder puts the door in that wall and the dressing lane
orients its yard, steps and lucam to match.

This lamp is NOT part of the 14-lamp roll — it is a road-shrine lamp beyond the town's warmth by design; beyond_warmth and the LAMP_ROLL=14 assert stand. landmarks.name: The Old Gate
landmarks.note: SHIPPED CANON (chapter1.js + STORY.md §1): 'the Old Gate' is what every line calls it; the SIGILS are the twin plates in the ground before it (built as separate props) that open only for two standing them together. Sealed at story start; opens in Ch1; downstream road+river beyond. | TERRAIN RULING 2026-08-01 (user): the Old Gate is the BOTTLENECK between the valley and two mountain cliff bluffs — its masonry built wall-to-wall into living rock so there is no way around; the river/brook exit the valley through the same pinch (a barred water-arch or alongside), and the shadowed gorge beyond IS the road toward Dellhollow. The north end of the valley funnels: forested bluffs converge, the wood climbs their slopes. Concept art variants in docs/qa/emberbrook/concepts/ (notch / valleys-end / ancient-seal), user choosing; blockout carries coarse bluff massing now, dressed cliffs follow the chosen concept. | DESIGN REFINEMENT 2026-08-01 (user): NOT a drain beside the gate — the river runs DIRECTLY PARALLEL to the road and flows UNDER the Old Gate itself: one wide structure spanning the whole notch, twin doors over the road, heavy DRAINAGE BARS (barred water-arches) over the river's passage beside them. Water passes through the gate; people must pass through the doors. GEOGRAPHY STATUS: the water-gap/hanging-valley reading is PROPOSED, not user-ratified — an overworld draft is being built so the user can judge it against their own vision of how the land leads to Dellhollow. Do not hard-bake overworld-dependent facts beyond this valley. | REFINEMENT 2 (user): the water passage is NOT an arch — arches are for humans. The drainage grate sits LOW, at water level only (a culvert grate slightly taller than the waterline), with plain coursed masonry wall above it. Only the road's doorway is arched. | SECLUSION RULING 2026-08-01 (user): the gate is TOO CLOSE to the town center. It moves to a genuinely secluded position — a quiet, wooded, incident-free stretch between the town's last warmth (the barn/dovecote area) and the court, designed as a MEASURED environment shift: village roofs fall out of sight past a threshold, lamp warmth ends at the barn, the forest closes in, then the sealed gate. Builder proposes the new gate/court/trailhead coordinates (notch, bluffs, and river tail move together) for the coordinator's stamp. | SECLUSION STAMP 2026-08-01: moved to [78,130] per the measured proposal — 87.1 m from the square (was 39.8), 41.1 m quiet stretch (was 0.0), roofs strict-zero from 38.9 m, seal re-proven 0.00/0.00/0 m2, notch 21.9 m rock-to-rock with the founded wall dead on gate-final.png. FINDING: seclusion is bought by the ROAD'S SHAPE, not its length — the road curves continuously and arrives 35 deg off the town's bearing (straight longer roads measured WORSE: the eye follows a clear road surface home). | CROSSING STAMP 2026-08-01 (user-ratified flavor 1): a second flag-stoned court on the VALLEY side of the gate, 8.0 m along the channel — the culvert-court crossing: the river runs under the paved court, the road crosses on the stone and leaves the gate on the EAST bank; no bridge, no span exists. _doc_parcels: PARCEL PASS 2026-08-01 (camera/data lane, coordinator authority delegated for this batch;
ch1-staging-audit.md stamp 4 + stamp 7). Two things were wrong and they were different things.
(1) MEMBERSHIP IS DERIVED FROM `bounds`, NOT FROM `members` — tools/townmap_derive.mjs and
viewer.html both call parcelsContaining(), which tests the landmark's position against the box.
`members` is the AUTHORED statement of the same fact, and the two had drifted a whole scale
apart: 24 landmarks were named in no `members` list and 5 fell inside no box at all. Every
`members` array below is now exactly what its bounds contain, so a reader and a tool cannot
disagree, and the four vista/dressing landmarks that sat outside every box (river-vista,
downstream-vista, far-rooftops-nw, hillside-cottages) are inside the parcel whose camera
already framed them — a vista is scenery OF a scene, and a landmark in no parcel has no scene
contract and therefore no sceneKey.
(2) SIX LANDMARKS SAT IN TWO PARCELS AT ONCE (washline-green, brook-bridge, bakery,
east-cottages, pips-den, poppy-stall) because neighbouring boxes overlapped across them. The
boxes were moved off each other along the axis that separates them and NOT resized around their
own contents: p-square's east face 82 -> 74 (nothing of the square's stands east of the item
shop at 74; the pond lane's footbridge and Pip's den do), p-homerow's south face 42 -> 47 (its
own southernmost member is Lake's home at y=48; the bakery and Poppy's stall at y~45 are the
square's), p-entrance's north face 30 -> 28, p-woodroad's north face 2 -> -2. Every landmark is
now in EXACTLY one parcel (was 6 doubled and 5 homeless), the sub-2 m gutters are gone, and 3 of
the 4 box overlaps with them. THE ONE THAT REMAINS IS STRUCTURAL AND IS LEFT STANDING WITH ITS
REASON: p-square n p-homerow over [46,47]..[54,56]. Home Row's lane and the square's west rim
interleave in x — the watermill at x=52.2 is Home Row's and the bakery at x=47.2 is the square's
— so no single plane separates them, and the box holds NO landmark either way. Closing it would
mean cutting the plaza's own floor out of its parcel to buy a warning.
(3) p-gateroad IS MINTED (deferred at the seclusion round, agreed then; audit stamp 7). The old
p-gatefield ran y 60..142 — 82 m from the tithe barn to the Old Gate, i.e. the town's last warm
building AND the deliberately unwarm court AND the 41.1 m of quiet road that the seclusion round
built to separate them, all under one scene contract. Chapter One stages on that road twice
(beat 27's refusal, beat 29's send-off), so it is a place, not a gutter. The split is made at
the road's own shape: p-gateroad holds the barn, the dovecote and the closed back lane (the
town's last warmth, the `beyond_warmth` rule's own boundary) and the corridor the road curves
through; p-gatefield keeps the court, the gate, the plates, the stile and the downstream vista.
The 2 m gutter between them at y=114..116 falls on open wooded road, which is where the village
roofs have been out of sight for 75 m already.

impliedScale._doc: USER RULING 2026-07-31: Emberbrook must READ as a lovely, lively town with deep history and a vibrant community — that is what a Heartlight DOES for a town — while chapter one stays focused and tight. Build the town to HINT at being much larger than the playable area: the player does not (and should not) have access to the whole town. Techniques, in canon order of preference: (1) non-walkable massing beyond every playable edge — further rooftops, chimney smoke, lit windows, hillside cottages, always composed into the camera frames; (2) lanes that visibly CONTINUE but are closed at the threshold (festival carts, stacked barrels, a hedge stile — soft, believable closures, never invisible walls); (3) at the Kindling Hour the square is CROWDED with background villagers — non-interactable or barely so; named cast are the interactive minority. The walk network stays exactly as tight as the parcels; the LOOK says big, the WALK says chapter one. | DENSIFICATION RULING 2026-08-01 (user, at 2x review): the village interior itself is TOO SPARSE — the large/populated/lively directive applies INSIDE the bounds, not only at the rim. Blockout-level implementation: deterministic INFILL of non-enterable background homes and structures filling the space between the playable lanes (clusters of 2-4 cottages with gardens, hedgerows, outbuildings, field strips) so every frame reads as a town, not houses on a lawn; closed lanes lead INTO visible clusters (a lane that ends at three more roofs says 'more town'); density gradient — thickest around Festival Square and Home Row, thinning toward the Gate Field and the wood. All infill is lm_-class massing at blockout, real dressed buildings at the district pass; never walkable, never enterable, GateGrid-gated off every lane and area. Target: from any playable lane, 2+ non-playable roofs visible in most directions. | REFINEMENT 2026-08-01 (user, from the mid-build snapshot): the infill overcorrected into unrealistic clutter — cottages packed wall-to-wall. A village cottage is a HOUSEHOLD: each infill home gets its own garden plot (hedge or fence), a fruit tree or two, a shed/woodpile, and a visible access path/track (non-walkable geometry is fine, but nobody builds a house with no way to reach it — tracks may join the real lanes or fade into implied ones). Spacing reads village-true: roughly 6-12 m between cottages, varied, with the FOREST filling between garden plots rather than more houses. Density comes from LIFE per household, not roofs per square metre. The 2+-roofs-visible target stands, met by depth and arrangement, not packing.

laneIncident._doc: USER RULING 2026-08-01: with distances doubled, lanes need MID-LANE INCIDENT to pace the walk — 'a cart, a shrine, a neighbor's fence' class of thing. Implementation is the district pass's dressing layer (post-blockout-ratification): every lane longer than ~15 m gets 1-2 incidents of domestic, familiar life — a handcart, a woodpile, a fence gate, a bench, laundry, beehives, a stile, apple crates — placed by SEARCH off the lane edge (never on walk surface), gated like all solids. LORE BUDGET NOTE: no invented shrine-institutions — in this town the lane punctuation with MEANING is Lake's lamp ring, which already exists; incidents are secular village life around it. Incidents cluster near homes and thin toward the Gate Field (the unwarm end thins to nothing).

forest._doc: USER RULINGS 2026-08-01: (1) THICKNESS — blockout stage: the forest is the village's CONTAINER, not a rim decoration. Thicken it hard: the wood presses in around and between the outer houses and along the main paths' outer sides, closes every horizon, and swallows the space beyond the infill clusters. Much of the perceived sparseness is missing forest. (2) QUALITY — dressing/bake stage, ON THE RADAR as a hard bar: the low-poly cone trees are placeholders only. The shipped vegetation must read natural/realistic to a modern-2026-game bar IN THE BAKED PLATES (pre-rendered backgrounds can afford film-weight trees at zero runtime cost — that is the architecture's whole advantage). GATE: before mass-producing the forest, a taste PROBE — one fixed camera, 2-3 tree treatments (geometry-node realistic / textured painterly / current stylized) — goes to the user, and the ratified treatment must keep Emberbrook and Dellhollow coherent as one game. | FARMLAND RULING 2026-08-01 (user): cleared land is welcome IF visibly CLAIMED for farming — the objection was never to open ground, it was to unclaimed emptiness between village and treeline. THE RULE: every acre between the village and the wood is either forest or WORKED land — field strips with boundaries (hedges/stone rows/fences), crop rows or autumn stubble, pasture, orchard extensions, haystacks — reading as somebody's livelihood. At blockout: field-parcel massing with boundary lines; at dressing: the crops, stubble, and farm clutter. No ambiguous green voids.

dressing._doc: USER-LOVED 2026-08-01, dressing-tier (district pass, not landmarks): stepping stones at one informal brook crossing; terraced kitchen gardens behind cottages; root-cellar doors in the Home Row rise; hay stooks + threshing floor by the tithe barn; lantern-maker's workbench (wicks, oil jars, glass) near the item shop; geese on the washline green; Mochi sunning ledges (waystone top, mill windowsill); drying racks + upturned skiff at the jetty. EXCLUDED BY RULING: wayside shrines (the Heartlight owns meaning) and fae-flavored anything (the Whisperwood's strangeness is Act 2 property).

coexistence._doc: USER RULING 2026-08-01 (the town-model review — supersedes styling details of earlier rulings where they conflict): 'This is a village that has stood itself up in the middle of a dense forest, and it coexists peacefully with nature rather than stripping away all nature to make space for its houses.' THREE CONSEQUENCES: (1) HOUSEHOLD BOUNDARIES lose the suburban trimmed-hedge vocabulary — irregular stone rows, split-rail/paling fragments, bramble clumps, PARTIAL enclosure; claimed, not manicured. (2) VILLAGE TREES: large individual trees scattered AMONG the houses and over the lanes — several species shapes and sizes (broadleaf crowns + slimmer forms alongside the forest conifers), so the wood visibly continues through the village. Blockout: varied canopy massing; QUALITY stays the dressing-stage bar. (3) THE SQUARE IS A CONTAINED ROOM: more buildings + trees closing the ring around Festival Square so it reads as its own space.
